description.narrative:
The Integrated Urban Basic Services Programme is aimed at supporting ongoing efforts by member states to achieve Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and other internationally agreed development frameworks such as the Paris Agreement, Sendai Framework and the New Urban Agenda (NUA) . Increased and equal access to basic services, sustainable mobility and public space is one of the outcome areas in “Domain of Change 1:” Reduced spatial inequality and poverty in communities across the urban-rural continuum” of the UN-Habitat Strategic Plan for the period 2020-2023. Urban basic services targeted at the urban poor and other vulnerable groups, including women, children and youth, older persons, persons with disabilities and migrants are equally critical to the achievement of the outcome areas of the other three domains of change, in particular Domain of Change 3: “Strengthened Climate Action and Improved Urban Environment”.
Experience has demonstrated that infrastructure and basic services investments, unless properly targeted, do not necessarily lead to better services for the urban poor. As highlighted in Paragraph 34 the New Urban Agenda, there is need to ensure that these services are responsive to the rights and needs of women, children and youth, older persons and persons with disabilities, migrants, indigenous peoples and local communities as appropriate, and others that are in vulnerable situations. Policies and programmes should be developed with and for urban dwellers, should prioritize the ones the more in need of them, and be mindful of the gender issues surrounding them. However, few local governments have a clearly defined urban development policy that prioritises basic services for the poor, not to speak of a city-wide strategy or plan for basic services in informal settlements. To address the above challenges, UN-Habitat’s Integrated Urban Basic Services Programme will prioritize policy and governance reform, strategic partnership with financing institutions, including the private sector, institutional development and capacity enhancement and pro-poor focus as central pillars for urban basic services provision.
UN-Habitat’s approach towards addressing the gaps in basic services of transport, energy water, sanitation and waste management is premised on better management of infrastructure assets as well as ensuring that the poor and vulnerable groups, including women, children and youth, older persons, persons with disabilities and migrants have access to a basic level of service. In line with the NUA, UN-Habitat looks to further refining its approach by developing mechanisms that allow the value of urbanisation itself to be harnessed for the improvement of these services, for example through transit oriented development that can open up economic opportunities for people, improve local tax revenues and improve access to public transport. Metropolitan approach to the integrated management of urban basic services Sustainable urban and territorial development is recognized in the NUA as essential to the achievement of sustainable development and prosperity for all (para 15a). The NUA also commits to strengthening the coordination role of national, subnational and local governments and their collaboration with other public entities and non-governmental organizations in the provision of social and basic services for all (para 21). In order to take advantage of the effects of urbanization on the progressive metropolization of cities, the programme will promote and incentivize governance and policies at the appropriate level, to carry out more efficient provision of urban basic services. It will support the strengthening of the capacity of subnational and local governments to implement effective local and metropolitan multilevel governance, across administrative borders, for the provision of public services (para 90). Differentiating the metropolitan approach is necessary to carry out adequate management at the territorial level of development of urban agglomerates with integrated governance and institutions that makes it possible to make the provision of urban basic services more equitable and inclusive according to the functionalities of the cities that make up the metropolis and for the control of urban expansion. Aligned with the NUA and crucial to the approach is the relationship between National Urban Policies and their local implementation. In the implementation of its previous UBSTF and WSTF programmes, UN-Habitat has engaged across the national, regional, and local community levels. UN-Habitat, for instance, was instrumental in introducing a new pro-poor water tariff regulation in Rwanda and introduced new building codes to enhance building energy efficiencies across several other African countries. UN-Habitat has also used National Urban Policies at the local and community levels by supporting the installation of water supply infrastructure which also demonstrated the innovative approach
